title: ～を込めて — putting ～ (feeling) into it
summary: Shows that an action is done with a feeling or wish put into it: “with all one’s heart, filled with ～.” It follows nouns of feeling such as 心, 気持ち, 愛 and 願い. 込める means to put something into it.

patterns.form: 気持ちを表す名詞＋を込めて＋動詞
patterns.gloss: noun of feeling + を込めて + action (感謝を込めて贈る)

body.p: Use it for acts aimed at someone or that you want to treasure, such as writing a letter, giving a gift or praying. 心を込めて, 感謝の気持ちを込めて and 願いを込めて are typical. It stresses that the action is done with real feeling.
To modify a noun use を込めた (心を込めた手紙). It is placed before the action: 〜を込めて、…. It also works with 力 (力を込めて押す), but then it means putting in physical effort, not emotion.

examples.ja: 心（こころ）を込（こ）めて手紙（てがみ）を書（か）いた。
examples.romaji: Kokoro o komete tegami o kaita.
examples.tr: I wrote the letter with all my heart.
examples.note: The most common phrase: 心を込めて.

examples.ja: 感謝（かんしゃ）の気持（きも）ちを込（こ）めて、花（はな）を贈（おく）った。
examples.romaji: Kansha no kimochi o komete, hana o okutta.
examples.tr: I gave flowers filled with feelings of gratitude.

examples.ja: 願（ねが）いを込（こ）めて、夜空（よぞら）の星（ほし）に祈（いの）った。
examples.romaji: Negai o komete, yozora no hoshi ni inotta.
examples.tr: Putting my wish into it, I prayed to the stars in the night sky.

pitfalls: A noun of feeling comes before it. Ordinary objects such as “机” do not work.
To modify a noun use を込めた: 心を込めた贈り物.
